sections.text: The Orionid meteor shower has become active as Earth travels through a trail of dust and debris shed by Halley's Comet. Tiny particles enter the atmosphere at around 41 miles per second, creating glowing trails that can briefly linger in the night sky.

Higher ocean temperatures and weaker winds helped storms gain strength rapidly.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The eastern Pacific experienced an active hurricane season with 22 named storms, 12 hurricanes, and 10 major hurricanes. Storms like Polo saw rapid intensification due to warm waters. Meanwhile, the Atlantic Ocean remained quiet with only one hurricane, Isaias.

sections.heading: Why it matters

timeline.text: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

gist: Monica Thomas experienced years of misdiagnoses before being diagnosed with lichen sclerosus.
The taboo around gynaecological health contributes to diagnostic delays and shame.
Clare Baumhaeur developed vulval cancer after decades of undiagnosed lichen sclerosus.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Women suffered from intimate itching, soreness, and blisters that were repeatedly dismissed as thrush, herpes, or other conditions. Monica Thomas and Clare Baumhaeur faced long delays, misdiagnoses, and physical pain before receiving a biopsy and a diagnosis of lichen sclerosus. Clare also developed vulval cancer.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Social taboo and embarrassment prevent people from speaking about gynaecological symptoms. A lack of awareness among healthcare professionals leads to delayed diagnoses, affecting mental health and, in some cases, leading to severe complications like cancer.

fivew: Monica Thomas, Clare Baumhaeur, and medical professionals.
Women spoke about their experiences with the misunderstood inflammatory condition lichen sclerosus.
To highlight diagnostic delays and the taboo surrounding gynaecological health.

sections.text: King Mohammed VI appointed Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as Morocco's first female prime minister. Her party, the Authenticity and Modernity Party, won the most seats in September's election and formed a four-party coalition holding 207 parliamentary seats.

sections.text: The appointment breaks a gender barrier, but has resurfaced conservative opposition and debate over women in leadership. sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: El Mansouri has not indicated whether she will push through family code reforms, leaving activists waiting to see if her government enacts actual change.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: At an event at Webster Hall, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and activist Ilana Glazer discussed artificial intelligence. Mamdani urged New Yorkers to reject the idea that AI adoption is inevitable and argued that public officials must hold technology firms accountable.

sections.text: Mamdani criticised the federal government for failing to regulate the sector, noting that national policy largely lets companies self-regulate. sections.text: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust faces three charges concerning the deaths of two young children who had sepsis. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: UK job openings fell by 21,000 to 691,000 during the three months to September, marking the lowest figure in more than five years. The steepest decline occurred within construction. sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Smaller firms are curbing recruitment because of climbing staffing overheads, including statutory wage increases and National Insurance changes, alongside higher energy bills. Although ministers cited employment resilience, youth unemployment reached 15.6%, leaving nearly one million young individuals outside work, education, or training.

gist: Covid inquiry report criticises government protection of care homes during the pandemic.
Failings included lack of PPE, moving untested hospital patients, and tough visiting restrictions.
Systemic weaknesses and blanket do not resuscitate orders caused severe harm.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Covid inquiry sixth report found that government action to protect care homes came too late, resulting in over 43,000 recorded deaths. The care sector was an afterthought, suffering from personal protective equipment shortages, unsafe hospital discharges without sufficient testing, and strict visiting restrictions that went too far. Additionally, GPs imposed unlawful blanket do not resuscitate orders.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Long-standing sector weaknesses, such as high staff vacancies, zero-hours contracts, and fragmented services, undermined the pandemic response. This exposed residents to severe health declines, caused deep distress among care staff, and strained mental health.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Eka Robotics raised a $150 million Series A funding round, achieving a valuation of $1.45 billion. Led by venture funds a16z and F-Prime, the startup has developed a manipulation architecture featuring a force-sensitive gripper and a new deep-learning model that astonishes roboticists with its speed and dexterity.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Unlike standard vision-language-action models, Eka relies on a vision-force-action model and reinforcement learning via physics simulation. This approach bypasses the limitations of human demonstration data, bridging the generality-performance gap and allowing robots to handle physical tasks rapidly and reliably.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Eka must transition successfully from lab demonstrations to real assembly lines with industrial customers, proving its hardware and techniques can endure continuous year-long operation across diverse tasks.

sections.text: NatWest plans to end its remote-first policy and mandate that employees work from the office at least two days a week. The BBC reported this affects 30,000 workers starting from February, while The Guardian reported the policy covers nearly 40,000 UK staff from February 2027. Unite attacked the change, arguing it disrupts thousands of lower-paid staff who currently attend twice a month.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Unite said the mandate increases travel and childcare costs during a cost-of-living squeeze, disproportionately affecting carers and disabled staff. gist: Nini Rodgers was a historian of Ireland’s involvement with slavery and abolition.
She published Ireland, Slavery and Anti-Slavery: 1612-1865 in 2007 after a four-decade career.
She was a dedicated lecturer at Queen’s University Belfast and a campaigner for change.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Historian Nini Rodgers died at the age of 86. Throughout a four-decade career at Queen’s University Belfast, she taught thousands of students and championed part-time night degrees. In 2007, she published her major work, Ireland, Slavery and Anti-Slavery: 1612-1865, challenging Ireland's self-image regarding the transatlantic slave trade. She was the daughter of Marie and the poet WR Rodgers, and partner to the late historian Jack Gray.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rodgers's research meticulously unmasked the reality of Ireland's involvement in slavery, replacing comforting fables with precise knowledge. She also shaped generations of historians and brought higher education to new kinds of people through her commitment to part-time students.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Esta High was taken to Leeds General Infirmary with a high temperature and vomiting. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Counter-terrorism police re-arrested two men on suspicion of assisting Iranian intelligence under the National Security Act 2023. The arrests follow a 27 September incident where three vans approached RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire. Petrol was discovered and nearby homes were evacuated, but officers found no explosive devices. Seven men have been arrested in total, with five remaining on bail.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Police consider Iranian state involvement highly likely. The prime minister told the Commons that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was almost certainly responsible, leading the US to withdraw 12 B-1 bombers from the base.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Specialist officers continue to examine the level and ambition of Iranian involvement, whilst five suspects remain on police bail.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Engineers at MIT and EPFL created a lightweight flapping-wing aerial-aquatic vehicle weighing under 300 grams. It uses a waterproof motor, flexible wings coated with nanoparticles, and a motorized tail. Tests in a water tank and Lake Geneva showed the robot can successfully transition from swimming underwater to flying in the air.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Moving through both air and water is difficult because water is much denser than air. This robot overcomes this challenge without needing feet. It could provide a cheaper way for oceanographers and marine biologists to sample hazardous aquatic areas.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The research team aims to design wings that can both turn and flap. They also plan to test the robot in turbulent conditions like choppy water and windy air before deploying it for ocean science research.

timeline.text: A reason to eat carbs

gist: Ketogenic diets may raise small intestine cancer risk while protecting the colon.
Dietary fat burning activates stem cells, promoting both gut repair and tumor growth.
Researchers emphasize that diet effects can differ greatly across the digestive tract.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A recent study investigated how a high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet affects the small intestine. Researchers discovered that mice fed this diet developed more small intestine tumors than control mice did. This occurred because burning dietary fat activates proteins that cause stem cells to multiply.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: While this diet can help with weight loss and protect against colon cancer, it carries a risk of tumor formation in the small intestine, showing that the same diet can have opposite effects in adjacent gut regions.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Scientists are continuing to investigate why adjacent parts of the gut experience such contrasting consequences from the same dietary fat pathway.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, driven largely by soaring petrol and diesel prices due to global conflicts. Meanwhile, government borrowing jumped to nearly £25bn.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The figures increase pressure on Chancellor John Healey ahead of his upcoming Budget, push up debt interest costs, and dictate higher welfare and pension increases.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Chancellor John Healey will deliver the Budget on 28 October, while the Bank of England's monetary policy committee meets next month.

gist: Websites across Europe take systems offline ahead of critical PHP updates.
Two critical vulnerabilities with severity ratings of 9.2 out of 10 affect PHP.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Finnish and Dutch governments took down websites ahead of a planned software update to the PHP programming language. Two critical vulnerabilities affecting versions from PHP 5 onwards were identified, prompting cyber-security agencies worldwide to issue warnings and advise organisations to apply fixes or take their websites offline.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: PHP powers a massive portion of the internet, including WordPress sites and hosting platforms. The vulnerabilities could allow unauthenticated remote code execution, letting hackers install malware, take down websites, or run their own code on affected servers.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Security patches are expected to be released, and organisations are urged to rapidly adopt the updates. Cloudflare reported seeing early attacks emerging, while experts warn that finding every instance of PHP running will be a major challenge.

timeline.text: 'Targeted' attack on much-loved MP leaves Australian town heartbroken

gist: Independent MP Helen Haines was severely injured in a targeted car attack in Wangaratta.
The community and national leaders expressed shock and support following the deliberate incident.
A local man appeared in court facing multiple charges as police consider further action.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Independent federal MP Helen Haines was struck by a car in a targeted and deliberate attack outside her Wangaratta office on Monday afternoon. She sustained severe injuries requiring both legs to be amputated after being airlifted to Melbourne. A local man was arrested at the scene after being pinned down by a witness, and appeared in court facing charges including intentionally causing harm, with police considering further charges such as attempted murder.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The tragedy has left the rural Victorian town of Wangaratta and the wider Australian community in profound shock. Haines is widely regarded as a well-liked, dedicated representative known for championing anti-corruption reform and regional infrastructure, making the violent incident deeply unsettling for locals who view her as a community fixture.

fivew: An independent MP was struck by a car in what police describe as a targeted attack.
Outside an office in Wangaratta, Victoria.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A former Conservative election candidate, Jack Ross, was suspended from the party after being filmed discussing contract killings and offering to broker services with a far-right activist. Ross was recorded by an undercover Al Jazeera journalist discussing prices for various violent acts, including murder, and introducing the reporter to a Glasgow criminal linked to the Ulster Volunteer Force.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The allegations involve serious criminal claims and links between far-right figures and political circles. Ross served as chief executive of Turning Point UK and had advised politicians, raising scrutiny over connections between fringe political groups and mainstream parties.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Conservative party suspended Ross with immediate effect pending an investigation. Additionally, Police Scotland announced they will be reviewing and assessing the documentary footage for any criminality.

sections.text: The addition of cross-platform modding could extend the lifespan of the game significantly, offering console players access to user-created modifications directly within the game.

sections.text: Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3 in the Champions League after trailing by two goals in the first half. sections.heading: Why it matters

sections.text: Racing Bulls is deciding its 2027 driver line-up between Liam Lawson, Arvid Lindblad, and Nikola Tsolov. sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The Racing Bulls decision marks the first time Helmut Marko is not choosing junior drivers. The Rwanda race plan faces accusations of sportswashing due to the country's human rights record and regional conflict involvement, though F1 defends the move as a positive economic and social opportunity.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Shareholders and executives will decide the Racing Bulls driver line-up. F1 continues to monitor security in the Middle East ahead of the final races, with an agreement in place to cover Imola's costs if it needs to step in as a venue.

gist: REDs is a serious health condition caused by low energy availability in sport.
Male athletes often suffer from REDs in silence due to stigma and lack of awareness.
Sports organisations are increasingly introducing education, health screenings, and preventative measures.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Athletes like Jake Smith and Brian Smith suffered severe injuries and health issues due to under-fuelling and REDs, driven by the sports culture of being as light as possible.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: REDs causes hormonal disruption, bone stress injuries, and long-term health problems. While women have menstrual cycles as a warning sign, men suffer more subtle symptoms and face stigma.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Experts and organisations are pushing for better education, nutrition advice, and mandatory health screenings to help athletes prevent and recover from REDs.

fivew: Male and female athletes in endurance and weight-sensitive sports.
Athletes are suffering from relative energy deficiency in sport, known as REDs.
Recently, as highlighted by a meta-analysis and ongoing athlete accounts.
Globally in sports, including elite and amateur levels.
Because of insufficient energy intake driven by the belief that lighter is faster and a lack of awareness.

gist: Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage felt shame after a 5-0 defeat by Brighton.
Sage admitted responsibility for the poor performance and said his future is uncertain.
Palace conceded three early goals in their heaviest loss to rivals Brighton since 1956.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Crystal Palace suffered a 5-0 defeat against Brighton after conceding three goals in the opening ten minutes. Manager Pierre Sage admitted responsibility for the performance, calling it his fault and stating he felt shame.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Sage faces uncertainty regarding his job after a tough start following his summer appointment. The heavy loss was Palace's worst against their rivals since January 1956, leaving them with the most goals conceded in the top flight.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Crystal Palace travel to Turkey to play Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday before hosting Newcastle in the Premier League on Sunday.

gist: Florian Wirtz starred as Liverpool beat Brentford to return to winning ways.
Wirtz created nine chances from open play, a notable Premier League statistic.
Pundits questioned the team's defensive shape and Wirtz's overall midfield role.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Liverpool came from behind to secure an away victory against Brentford in the Premier League. Florian Wirtz created nine chances from open play, the most in a single Premier League game for six seasons, helping the visitors score twice in the second half after Brentford were reduced to 10 men.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory moved Liverpool up to fifth in the table. However, analysts debate whether deploying Wirtz as a number 10 leaves the team too open defensively and structurally vulnerable.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Liverpool face Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday amid concerns over a demanding schedule and fresh injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong.

gist: Celtic secured a seven to one victory against Hearts at Celtic Park.
Hearts suffered from severe defensive errors and psychological collapse during the match.
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill gained a much-needed win and praised his attacking players.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Celtic defeated Hearts seven to one in a match featuring early goals and multiple defensive mistakes by the visitors.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The emphatic win provides Celtic and manager Martin O'Neill with a significant boost after recent difficult periods.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Celtic aims to maintain this positive momentum over the long road ahead in the league campaign.

fivew: Martin O'Neill's Celtic team and Wouter Vrancken's Hearts team
Celtic defeated Hearts with a score of seven to one.
Hearts suffered from comically bad use of the ball and individual errors.
